products.name: InternLM (Shanghai AI Lab)
products.note: Chinese open-source LLM; academic research; cross-border data review advised

reading.body:
Shanghai AI Laboratory is a government-affiliated research institution in China operating InternLM, an open-source large language model positioned for academic research across Chinese universities and scientific applications.

The laboratory's stated focus spans model capability, embodied robotics, and AI safety frameworks, with recent emphasis on science-oriented systems that integrate language models, specialist agents, and physical automation. This portfolio suggests a research strategy prioritizing broad capability development rather than any single domain constraint. The 2026 announcement of AI-for-science results and a scientific discovery platform indicates the institution is testing large models as infrastructure for experimental workflows, from hypothesis through validation.

What matters for AI infrastructure is that Shanghai AI Laboratory operates within China's university and research ecosystem, not as a commercial infrastructure builder or power provider. The laboratory contributes to model capability and research methodology but does not control the compute, buildings, or power grids that determine how quickly those capabilities can scale. It represents the downstream user of infrastructure, not the constraint that binds it.

The data does not cover the laboratory's budget, its access to compute hardware, or the power requirements of its training and inference systems. Without those facts, the connection between its research ambitions and the infrastructure constraints that may or may not enable them remains unmeasured.

profile_text.body:
Shanghai AI Laboratory is a government-run, non-profit artificial intelligence research lab, according to the record held on it. Its website describes it as recruiting young researchers worldwide in artificial intelligence, large models, embodied intelligence, trustworthy AI, AI for Science, basic platforms, the innovation chain, and management support, with the stated aim of working toward AGI. Since 2022, the lab says it has run a joint doctoral training program with more than ten leading universities, among them Peking University, Tsinghua University, Fudan University, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Tongji University, the University of Science and Technology of China, and Zhejiang University.

Its best known product line is InternLM, a Chinese open-source large language model tracked in the chat and general LLM category, with a note flagging academic research use and advising cross-border data review. The site also describes a family of Shusheng models and platforms: the Shusheng Duanyan science discovery platform, which it says was upgraded and fully opened as a full-stack service at the 2026 Pujiang Innovation Forum; the Shusheng physical world model W0; the Shusheng science multimodal large model S2; and Intern-Robotics, an embodied intelligence full-stack engine. It describes a general and specialist fusion technical system in three layers, and an AI-45 degree balance law for safety and performance, with the lab exploring a causal path toward trustworthy AGI.

Professor Zhou Bowen, named on the site, proposed the idea that scientific research is the next programming, building on the AGI4S six questions raised at the previous year's Pujiang Innovation Forum. At the 2026 WAIC science frontier forum, the lab says it released ten joint innovation results with partners in life sciences, materials science, and deep space astronomy. The site also mentions a North Star talent program for global recruitment.
